reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume roughly doubled since August (E-05: 610→590→1180→1260/month) because the majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025, E-02) are tied to ACTUAL meter reads, not estimate substitutions — ruling out tariff changes (E-01) and making AMI/field read-capture gaps insufficient as the dominant cause. Current evidence best supports that a change to billing import validation rules around August (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE) is causing otherwise-valid ACTUAL reads to be rejected or mishandled during billing import, producing incorrect bills that customers then dispute; a secondary minority of disputes (1240 ESTIMATED-read bills) is driven by a field-staffing route-completion shortfall (0.88 vs 0.95 target, E-03).
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume roughly doubled since August 2026 (610→590→1180→1260/month, E-05), spanning 1240 ESTIMATED-read and 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (E-02). Account-level evidence confirms billing-import rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, E-12), which compares raw unscaled register values to 12-month m3 history, misclassifies firmware-v4.2 meters' 0.1 m3-unit readings (E-13) as high-consumption outliers and rejects them under REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION at import (E-11); this pathway produced exactly 1184 affected accounts, all billed ESTIMATED (E-14), accounting for the bulk of the ESTIMATED-read disputes. This confirmed mechanism structurally always yields ESTIMATED billing and therefore cannot explain the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills — the larger share of the surge — whose cause is distinct from BV-17/firmware-v4.2 and not yet established by evidence (E-14).
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
